speaker: Patient
text: 18-month-old boy. The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. The parents report that there was no obvious injury or incident at the park that could have led to the swelling. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Hemophilic Arthropathy (likely Hemophilia A or B).

Given the patient's age, spontaneous knee swelling without trauma, and the specific family history of similar issues, this strongly suggests a bleeding disorder. I will now request results for the Coagulation Panel (PT, aPTT) and Factor Assay to confirm the specific deficiency. REQUEST TEST: Coagulation_Panel, Factor_Assay.
